Subject: Brightlane VPC integration — control/data handshake and reference diagrams

Hi Samira + Evan,

Thanks for the kickoff earlier — Per our readout I pulled together a concise reference pack that describes how Redwood's control plane will interoperate with Brightlane's on-prem data plane. The attached PDF contains a simplified sequence:

- Control plane components (auth, model registry, routing) will sit in a managed VPC peered to Brightlane's transit VPC.
- Data plane inference pods will live in Brightlane's tenant cluster. KV cache and model artifacts use an S3-compatible gateway over the peering link.
- Egress expectations: minimal outbound to Redwood telemetry endpoints; all inference payloads remain inside Brightlane unless explicit opt-in for logging.

Action items I want to confirm in this thread:
1) Brightlane's preferred CIDR ranges for the peering (we've sketched 10.40.0.0/16 for control plane access).
2) Which subnets will allow outbound HTTPS to telemetry.redwood.ai (ports 443) and whether a proxy is required.
3) Any gov/reg constraints on HSM/KMS calls — if your KMS is on-prem we can route KMS requests through the peering.

I've attached: reference-diagram-brightlane-onprem-2025-06-11.png (mapping), brightlane-vpc-egress-matrix.xlsx (per-service egress matrix), and brightlane-vpc-controlplane-data-handshake-v1.pdf (sequence + short checklist).

If you prefer a short call to walk the diagram, happy to set 30 minutes — propose Thu 6/12 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Evan, Samira — thanks, that's helpful. Short replies inline and updated attachments uploaded to the Drive link.

- CIDR: 10.40.128.0/18 works; we've updated the diagram to show the explicit /18 block and changed the control-plane NAT ranges. See reference-diagram (v2) on Drive.
- Proxy: Redwood's control plane components can route telemetry via your proxy; we'll need a static outbound IP range from your proxy to allow our pull-based artifact fetches.
- mTLS to KMS: yes, Redwood supports mutual TLS to customer-managed KMS endpoints. We have two options: 1) route Redwood KMS calls over the peering to your KMS endpoint, or 2) use a lightweight Vault agent within your tenant cluster to broker keys locally. The Vault-agent option reduces cross-VPC secrets traffic and keeps crypto ops entirely inside Brightlane.

I've also added a short checklist in the PDF under "Pre-cutover checks" with items for firewall rules, egress proxy ACLs, and KMS certificate exchange steps.

If the 10:00 PT slot still works I can send the calendar invite — Jonas and Camila will join to walk the control plane routing and runtime placement.

Best,
Neha

Great to see alignment — quick technical notes from my side before the call:

1) NAT and ephemeral ports: ensure your egress proxy preserves source ports for long-lived artifact downloads. Our runtime opens concurrent connections for shard downloads, and port translation can cause retransmits if not preserved.

2) Flow logs & audit: we propose enabling VPC flow logs for the peering subnets with a 14-day retention, shipped to your SIEM (we'll accept a read-only token for verification). This satisfies our compliance checklist without shipping payloads.

3) Fallback model variants: we'll stage a quantized variant in Brightlane's on-prem object store (read-only) so that if peering degrades we continue serving with a smaller model locally. This is in the "Operational fallback" section of the PDF.

Agenda for the 30m call (Jonas = host):
- 0-5m: Introductions + scope
- 5-15m: Walk reference diagram and peering details (Neha + Camila)
- 15-25m: Firewall/proxy/KMS integration checklist (Evan + Joseph)
- 25-30m: Next steps + cutover timeline & owner assignments

I'll send the 10:00 PT invite — please accept and upload any raw network configs (BGP peering ASN, transit gateways) to the Drive folder ahead of the meeting.

Cheers,
